## Problem / why
Direct database queries and file reads bypass security checks, risking cross-tenant memory leakage and inconsistent writes.

## Goal & value
Build the central Memory Orchestrator as the single governed gateway for all memory operations with strict tenant and project ACL enforcement.

## Reference Documents
- `docs/Product_Forge_Agent_Memory_Architecture_Integration.md#section-7`
- `docs/Product_Forge_Agent_Memory_Architecture_Integration.md#section-14`

## In scope
- Unified gateway interface (Put, Get, Search, Delete, Validate, Consolidate).
- Multi-tenant isolation and Row-Level Security (RLS) enforcement.
- Project and user ACL boundary checks.
- Negative penetration tests verifying zero cross-tenant leakage.

## Out of scope
- Direct bypass of the orchestrator by individual agent workers.

## Definition of Done
- Leakage penetration tests pass with zero cross-boundary exposure.

## Verification
Structured `acceptance_criteria` is the single source of truth for verification.

NIT: Logic Duplication: The simultaneous existence of `core/memory_orchestrator.py` and `go/pfmemory/orchestrator.go` suggests logic drift and unclear component ownership.
MAJOR: Observability (CL-010): No definition for telemetry, metrics, or logging of intercepted operations and ACL denials, preventing auditability of the security gateway.
Availability (Checklist 2): Design lacks a failure-mode definition (e.g., fail-closed) and circuit-breaking logic for when the underlying storage provider is unreachable.
MINOR: Dry-run Mode (Checklist 4): Destructive operations like 'Delete' and 'Consolidate' lack a mandatory dry-run/report mode to bound the blast radius of automated operations.
Reversibility (Checklist 1): No verified backup or state-reversal path is defined for the 'Consolidate' operation, which may destructively modify memory history.
BLOCKER: Language Rule Violation: "Build the central Memory Orchestrator" constitutes new shipped logic; implementation in `core/memory_orchestrator.py` violates the Go-only requirement for new logic.
Security Posture (CL-011): Design fails to specify or enforce the runtime role posture (NOSUPERUSER/NOBYPASSRLS), which is mandatory to ensure RLS integrity and prevent bypass.
Parameterized Binding (CL-013): Missing requirement for constant-time token comparison and strictly parameterized tenant binding in the gateway interface to prevent leakage.
SUMMARY: The design establishes a critical security gateway but violates core engineering standards regarding language selection and mandatory security postures (RLS).
Top risks include potential RLS bypass due to undefined role permissions and a total lack of operational observability for security events.

NIT: All three ACs cite the same evidence artifact and candidate_sha a9425dfd; Gate 2 must replace these with distinct per-suite test evidence (partially acknowledged in pack learnings).
Audit "safe record ID" retention/redaction policy is unspecified while privacy_compliance is marked N/A; a short retention statement would close the gap.
MAJOR: AC-1 "all operations" is unenforceable as designed: only go/edpsvc call sites are wired, with no stated arch-test/static check proving no other code path reaches go/memory or datastore directly (bypass is merely out_of_scope, not prevented).

Authorization-vs-mutation ordering for Delete is ambiguous: C-3 says deletes "verify tenant, project, and ACL after repository access"; the design must pin read-verify-then-delete (or tenant-filtered delete) or a cross-tenant row could be mutated before denial.

Search result post-filtering is unspecified: the rls_tenant section rechecks "after every single-record read" only, yet AC-2/coverage claim filters "on every operation" — per-hit tenant/project/ACL revalidation of multi-record Search results must be explicit.

Search bound contradicts the approved NFR: NFR says k <= 100 and performance says default 20, but config_contract allows PF_MEMORY_MAX_SEARCH_K = 1..1000 with default 100; the contract cannot be met as written.
MINOR: RLS role-posture test runs only "when a test DSN is configured"; without a required CI DSN the CL-011 NOSUPERUSER/NOBYPASSRLS evidence is silently skipped.

PF_MEMORY_PRINCIPAL contract is internally contradictory (precedence "server" vs env key; empty→"deny in production" vs default→"existing server principal"); precedence and production-empty behavior need one rule.
AC-3's "four negative leakage suites" are not enumerated as four distinct named tests; C-4 lists TestLeakageSuites as both negative_test and positive_test.
D-1 hides legacy project-empty rows with no migration owner/ticket and no metric for filtered-out rows, so silent data invisibility is undetectable in production.
Rollback trigger "roll back on denial spikes" has no threshold, alert, or lead-time defined (checklist 2 availability).
No statement that pfmemory metrics reuse the existing edpsvc metrics registry/namespace; duplicate metric definitions would break dashboards (checklist 10 reuse).
SUMMARY: Design is now Go-only, fail-closed, and observability-aware; prior blockers are properly dispositioned. Top risks: AC-1 has no anti-bypass enforcement, delete/search authorization ordering and per-hit filtering are not pinned, and the k-bound NFR contradicts the config contract. Resolve the MAJOR items before Gate 1.5; no BLOCKERs remain.

C-7 (bypass enforcement) is owned by and lives in go/pfmemory/bypass_test.go but its control targets go/edpsvc call sites; a static check inside the pfmemory module cannot reliably see edpsvc's repository usage, and it will not run on edpsvc-only changes, weakening AC-1's "intercepts all operations" proof.
